topic: State Legislature: Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council
description: Part VI of the Indian Constitution deals with the State Legislature. It is the supreme law-making body at the state level, which can be either unicameral or bicameral depending on the state's specific requirements.

sections.title: Constitutional Framework and Types
sections.description: Constitutional provisions related to the formation of the State Legislature and the basic structure of its houses.

key_concepts.explanation: A system comprising only one house, the Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha), along with the Governor. A majority of Indian states follow this system.
A system comprising two houses: the Legislative Assembly and the Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad), with the Governor functioning as an integral part.

polity_articles.details: Defines that every State Legislature shall consist of the Governor and either one or two Houses.

polity_articles.provision: Abolition or Creation of Legislative Councils in States.
polity_articles.details: The Parliament can create or abolish a Legislative Council by a simple majority, provided the state's Legislative Assembly passes a resolution to that effect by a special majority.

important_facts.fact: Currently, only 6 states in India have a bicameral legislature: Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana.

sections.title: Legislative Assembly: Composition and Election
sections.description: Rules regarding the composition, tenure, and electoral process of the Legislative Assembly, also known as the Lower House.

key_concepts.explanation: The popular house of the state whose members are directly elected by the people through territorial constituencies.
The principle that all adult citizens (18 years or above) of the state possess the right to vote in the Legislative Assembly elections.

polity_articles.details: Specifies that the Legislative Assembly of each state shall consist of not more than 500 and not less than 60 members.

polity_articles.provision: Qualification for membership of the State Legislature.
polity_articles.details: A person must be a citizen of India and not less than 25 years of age to be eligible for membership in the Legislative Assembly.

important_facts.fact: The states of Sikkim (32), Goa (40), and Mizoram (40) are exceptions to the minimum strength rule of 60 members.
The normal tenure of the Legislative Assembly is 5 years, but it can be extended by the Parliament by 1 year at a time during a National Emergency.

sections.title: Legislative Council: Composition and Electoral College
sections.description: Membership criteria and the indirect election process of the Legislative Council, also known as the Upper House.

key_concepts.explanation: The Legislative Council is a continuing chamber and is not subject to dissolution. One-third (1/3rd) of its members retire every 2 years, making the tenure of an individual member 6 years.

polity_articles.details: The total number of members in the Legislative Council shall not exceed one-third (1/3rd) of the total strength of the state's Legislative Assembly, and shall not be less than 40.

key_associations.associated_with: Elected by MLAs and Local Bodies
key_associations.extra_info: One-third are elected by members of municipalities/district boards, and another one-third by the members of the Legislative Assembly.
Nominated from among persons having special knowledge in Literature, Science, Art, Cooperative Movement, and Social Service.
One-twelfth are elected by 3-year standing graduates, and another one-twelfth by teachers of at least secondary school level with 3 years of experience.

important_facts.fact: To become a member of the Legislative Council, a person must be at least 30 years of age.

sections.title: Legislative Powers and Procedures
sections.description: Comparison of the powers of both houses regarding the passage of ordinary and money bills.

key_concepts.explanation: Can be introduced in either House. Unlike the Parliament, there is no provision for a Joint Sitting in the state legislature to resolve a deadlock between the two Houses.
Can only be introduced in the Legislative Assembly and strictly requires the prior recommendation of the Governor.

polity_articles.provision: Restriction on powers of Legislative Council as to Bills other than Money Bills.
polity_articles.details: The Legislative Council can delay an ordinary bill for a maximum of 4 months (3 months in the first instance and 1 month in the second instance).

polity_articles.provision: Special procedure in respect of Money Bills.
polity_articles.details: The Legislative Council can delay a Money Bill for a maximum of 14 days, after which it is deemed to be passed by both Houses.
The Governor can give assent, withhold assent, return the bill (if not a Money Bill), or reserve the bill for the consideration of the President.
